rationale: The source holds three independent obligations, joined in one THEN. (1) The corpus renders with asciidoctor, and an attributable build failure is FAIL. (2) Every internal cross-reference resolves, and an unresolvable one is FAIL. Its evidence, fix and external-link exception differ from (1). (3) When the validator cannot observe (absent toolchain, crashed renderer, unreadable tree, unattributable failure), the verdict is COULD_NOT_CHECK, which blocks, and never PASS, FAIL or NOT_APPLICABLE. Part 3 has a different trigger (toolchain or renderer state, not document content) and a different fix (make the renderer runnable, do not edit docs). The source calls this verdict distinction 'the point of this rule'. The source makes (1) and (2) jointly mandatory, so the two parts require each other. Both also require (3), so an unexamined corpus can never pass either one. Round 3: parts (1) and (2) now activate on every docs_validation run, unconditionally; findings only classify the verdict and are no longer activation prerequisites. Strict disposition is stated directly in every part and each part also requires the shared strict-disposition policy; could-not-check also requires the shared unknown-not-exempt policy.

The reference implementation is asciidoctor (Ruby), not a pure Python renderer, because unresolvable internal references must be VALIDATION FAILURES and the Python options detect them weakly. A Ruby runtime in CI is the cost, accepted deliberately (spec 2 §9 Decision 4).

parts.given: The docs validator is run over the corpus.
parts.when: The toolchain is absent, the renderer crashes, the tree is unreadable, or a build failure cannot be attributed to a specific document.

parts.why: The verdict distinction is the point of this rule and the thing most likely to be got wrong. This repository has had the bug in at least three places (#1745, #1774, #1716).
evidence: When the toolchain is absent or the failure is unattributable, the docs_capability report shows COULD_NOT_CHECK (not PASS, FAIL or NOT_APPLICABLE) and the gate blocks
verifier_detail: unattributable_failure: a render failure the capability cannot pin to a document, such as a crashed renderer, an unreadable tree, or a toolchain that is not installed. It is reported as COULD_NOT_CHECK, which BLOCKS.

Verdict mapping: an ABSENT toolchain, or a build failure the capability cannot attribute to a specific document, is COULD_NOT_CHECK: never PASS and never FAIL (spec 2 §3 'What the capability owes core', and §7).

THE VERDICT DISTINCTION IS THE POINT OF THIS RULE, and the thing most likely to be got wrong. 'There is no obligation here' (NOT_APPLICABLE, permits) and 'I could not see whether the obligation was met' (COULD_NOT_CHECK, blocks) must never collapse into one another.
An unresolvable lookup must remain DATA: a named, reportable state that reaches the report, never an empty clean result.

Defect lineage. Spec 2 §3 states this emphatically because the repository has the bug in at least three places. In #1745, coach.pr.merge-blocks-on-pre-smoke-close degrades to advisory on a lookup failure and REPORTS IT AS A PASS. In #1774, 'no mirror found' is read as 'nothing to lose', and 15 nodes are invisible to the succession guard. In #1716, checks pass when they cannot observe, and C011 compares the store against itself.
Severity 1. Disposition strict: fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
